title: Close the roller clamp on an IV line left running free, holding the clamp still while the wheel is rolled shut
justification: Registered nurses (O*NET 29-1141, about 3.3M) and licensed practical nurses (29-2061, about 0.63M) close an IV set's roller clamp every time a set is primed, loaded, changed or stopped. A gravity line found running unclamped (free flow) is a recognised medication-error hazard. The clamp is a 54 mm, 6 g plastic body riding loose on soft tubing, so rolling its wheel with one hand only pushes the clamp and line along. A nurse pinches the body in one hand and thumbs the wheel with the other; a robot needs two grippers for the same thing.
fault: A primed set hangs from a 1 L bag on a pole and runs across the overbed table to the cannula in a manikin's forearm. Its roller clamp lies on the table wide open, with the wheel at the open end, and the line is running free.
instruction: Close the roller clamp on this IV line.
objects: IV pole stub, fixed (as in the accepted Alaris task), at x 45, y -25, with a 1 L saline bag (custom mesh, 1.05 kg, fixed on its hook) and a rigid drip chamber. Administration-set tubing: PVC, 4.1 mm OD, a 60 cm capsule chain on the table (pattern from the accepted Alaris task, credited), anchored at the drip chamber outlet and at the cannula hub. Roller clamp, custom mechkit: a white polypropylene body 54 x 18 x 15 mm (mass raised to 15 g for the solver), welded to one tubing link and lying wheel-up at x 27, y -4. Its blue 11 mm wheel runs on a prismatic joint along a 22 mm sloped track, held by friction (about 4 N to roll), and counts as closed within 2 mm of the narrow stop. Manikin forearm with a taped cannula, fixed, at x 24, y 22. The bench is the overbed table. Distractors (SimReady): syringe_a01 at x 16, y -22; bandage_medical_a01 at x 38, y 8; thermometer_fever_a01 at x 15, y 10.
skill: Fine two-handed manipulation. One gripper pins or pinches the 18 mm clamp body against the table near its tail. The other drives the 11 mm wheel 22 mm along its track with a fingertip, without lifting or dragging the clamp, which would tug the line on the patient's cannula.
scoring: From poses and the wheel's joint (real trial: a photo of the wheel against the clamp's moulded stop). Whole-run latch P: the line between clamp and cannula pulled taut (its end-to-end length within 2 cm of its slack length), or the cannula-end link moved more than 5 mm. End: grippers 2 cm or more from clamp and tubing, everything still for 1 s. Score 0 if P is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 wheel within 2 mm of the closed stop; 0.4 wheel 60 percent or more of the way but not closed; 0 otherwise. Kinking or pinching the tube elsewhere earns nothing.
nearest: 'Load an IV set into an Alaris pump module' (accepted) seats the same kind of set and presses its safety clamp into a recess. Also 'Add IV bag spiking and drip-chamber priming task' (revising) and 'Scrub the IV connector's hub for 15 seconds' (accepted). No existing task works a roller clamp's wheel.
risks: The parts are at the gripper's limit (2 cm pads, an 11 mm wheel, an 18 mm body), and the two grippers work within 5 cm of each other. The soft tubing chain must stay stable with a light clamp welded to it. Reviewers may treat it as part of the IV-set family already covered. Fluid flow is not simulated, so closure is judged by the wheel position only.
